query: Which material can be used for enhanced catalytic activity and durability toward HER and HOR, and why?

generation.hypothesis: We hypothesize that doping Ni-based catalysts with Fe will enhance catalytic activity and durability for both the hydrogen evolution (HER) and hydrogen oxidation (HOR) reactions, relative to undoped Ni.
generation.intervention: Introduce Fe dopants into the Ni lattice at various concentrations (e.g., 0–10 wt%).
generation.conditions: Operate in alkaline media (0.1 M KOH) at 25–60 °C to evaluate HER and HOR performance; maintain identical solution pH across all samples.
generation.structural_mediator: Fe incorporation modifies Ni’s local electronic structure and lattice geometry, potentially creating more active sites for proton adsorption and catalysis.
generation.mechanism: The dopant-induced electronic modifications reduce the reaction free-energy barrier, boosting overall catalytic turnover and helping preserve surface integrity under repeated redox cycles.
generation.predicted_outcome: An approximate 20–30 mV reduction in overpotential at 10 mA cm−2 and improved stability after extended cycling, compared to undoped Ni.
generation.baseline: Undoped Ni catalyst tested under the same conditions.
generation.boundary: Benefits diminish at Fe doping levels above ~10 wt%; acidic media may yield lower enhancements than alkaline conditions.
generation.uncertainty: Durability over long-term operation and any influence of large-scale synthesis methods remain underexplored and require further study.

falsification_experiment.design: Conduct rotating disk electrode (RDE) tests on both Ni-Fe and pure Ni catalysts at multiple Fe doping levels under identical conditions. Measure visible shifts in polarization curves and Tafel slopes over repeated cycles.
measurements: Tafel slopes for HER and HOR
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If Ni-Fe catalysts do not exhibit statistically significant reductions in overpotential or improvements in stability compared to undoped Ni, the hypothesis is invalidated.
